Subject: Enablement: access exit criteria & credential/VPC peering plan

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for committing time for the eval. As discussed in the MAP workshop, we want to lock the environment access items and an explicit close timeline so your engineers can validate end-to-end in a production-like setup. Below is the minimal enablement checklist we need to hit to move from trial -> acceptance: 

1) Org creation & admin invite (VitalHealth org in Redwood Console) — we need the primary admin email(s).
2) API keys: one short-lived key for load-testing, one scoped key for evaluation. Request form attached.
3) IP allowlist: list of public IP ranges for your staging agents; we will provide our egress ranges for peering prep.
4) VPC peering: template + proposed maintenance window (we prefer a 2-hour window for the test cutover).
5) Data retention/SLA check — quick confirmation you’re happy with the default 30-day logs for this eval.

Target close timeline (MAP-driven):
- Today (Jun 29): agree on contacts, provide IP ranges, sign off on peering template.
- Jun 30–Jul 1: Redwood provisions org and temporary API keys; VitalHealth schedules peering slot.
- Jul 2: Cutover test (connectivity + a short smoke test).
- Jul 5: Validation window complete; acceptance decision.

Could you confirm the ops contact and a preferred peering window? I’ve attached the API key request form and a blank VPC peering template to speed things up.

Next steps for us internally: I’ll loop Priyom and Karthik to pre-provision the org and start the API key workflow after we get your IP list.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
